title: Early Thaumaturgy
summary: The state of Tremere blood magic in the early 13th century.

claims.text: In the two centuries since Tremere and the founders became vampires, most of their work has gone into recovering their magic as the new blood art called Thaumaturgy.
They are still adapting Hermetic arts and rituals to it, with little true invention beyond the blood-centred Rego Vitae path.
Within a few decades the House breaks with the Order of Hermes for good, losing the great Hermetic libraries, and from the mid-13th century Thaumaturgy goes its own way.

title: Rego Magica
summary: A rare path for turning Hermetic techniques into blood magic.

claims.text: Tremere, Goratrix and Etrius created the path to convert Hermetic techniques into Thaumaturgy, and Tremere keeps knowledge of it tightly held to stop juniors inventing paths their master does not know.
It also gives strong weapons against enemy magi; the Inner Circle knows of it, though not all of them can use it.
Rego Magica and Perdo Magica are offered only at the Storyteller’s discretion, and Perdo Magica is the more widely known.

title: Researching new rituals
summary: How thaumaturges create rituals at Ceoris.

claims.text: After at least thirty hours a week of research, the thaumaturge rolls Intelligence + Occult at difficulty 5 and then performs the new ritual; normally Rego Magica must exceed the ritual’s level by at least 2.
Depending on both rolls, the ritual may be impossible to create, may be retried later, or may work without the creator fully understanding it.
A new ritual is known only to its maker until taught or written down, and a written copy can be stolen; Ceoris researchers share secrets only to seal alliances, settle feuds or pay debts.
Several researchers can pool their efforts: each subtracts 1 from Rego Magica and the results are added, with one researcher making the rolls.

title: The bronze head
summary: A Tremere ritual that pulps a prisoner’s brain for answers.

claims.text: The ritual builds a speaking bronze head that draws memories from a prisoner, even long-buried or magically hidden ones, regardless of the victim’s will.
The ritualist rolls Intelligence + Occult against the victim’s Stamina + Fortitude at difficulty 9, and each net success gives one useful piece of information.
Mortals and ghouls without Fortitude die; a vampire needs three successes on Stamina + Fortitude at difficulty 9 to end in torpor, five to be merely Incapacitated, and ghouls need five just to live.
Each head has a cold little persona of its own; the one at Ceoris, Paracelsus, fawns on its maker Mendacamina.

title: Creating Gargoyles
summary: The ritual for stitching Gargoyles from Cainites.

claims.text: The thaumaturge sews together parts of Cainites into a humanoid form, each part lending traits according to old medical lore, such as the heart for courage and the eyes for perception.
The roll is Intelligence + Occult at difficulty 9, plus one for each donor after the first, or 4 less with an unliving womb; a single success creates a Gargoyle character.
The ritual costs 5 blood points for each Cainite used, plus 5 more for a fertile Gargoyle, and no Gargoyle can be made beautiful.
The Tremere stop making Gargoyles after the slave revolt and later promise never to revive the art, though the instructions are hidden rather than destroyed.

title: Malign Humors
summary: Rituals that brew temporary enhancements for Gargoyles.

claims.text: Virstania Malgorzata and Goratrix devised rituals for magical humors that boost Gargoyles for a time but exact a price afterwards.
Each humor needs exotic ingredients suited to its nature, such as a venomous snake for a humor granting a poisonous bite.
The humor cannot simply be drunk: a machine drains much of the Gargoyle’s vitae, mixes it with the humor and returns it by transfusion.
